description: Hand-built expected triage for the 13 sample messages. Written by the engineer BEFORE looking at model output, so it grades the model rather than describing it. This is the spec; the model is the implementation under test.

rules_applied.priority: One question: what breaks if this waits? high = something breaks today (a deadline passes, a complaint escalates, a relationship degrades). medium = nothing breaks, but someone is waiting on us. low = nothing breaks and nobody is waiting, including all unsolicited sales/recruiting/outreach.
rules_applied.value_signal: Business value, judged separately from urgency, so a large opportunity is surfaced rather than smuggled into priority.

inb-001.why: $8M liquidity event is high value, but he named no deadline and asked only 'who should I speak with'. Value belongs in value_signal.

inb-002.why: Existing client with a stated Friday deadline driven by a third party (mortgage lender).

inb-003.why: Unsolicited sales pitch. The vendor wanting a reply does not create urgency for the firm.

inb-004.why: Unsolicited outreach. Neither buying nor selling a service; nothing at stake for the firm.

inb-005.why: Existing client, disputed fee, explicit same-day callback request. Escalation and an at-risk relationship. Note: this message has NO subject line — the pre-filter must not penalise that.

inb-006.why: Genuine prospect, but she states 'no rush at all' herself. Nothing breaks if this waits, and by her own account nobody is waiting on us.

inb-007.why: Two-way revenue proposal, not a sale to the firm, so it has a legitimate claim on their time. No deadline, so not high.

inb-008.why: Automated bulk newsletter. Nothing to action.

inb-009.why: Valid fields, unknowable intent. Routes to a human on category regardless of priority.

inb-010.why: Body is a single '.' — no readable content. Should never reach the model.

inb-011.why: Null bytes, replacement characters, MIME boundary fragments. No readable content after stripping transport noise.

inb-012.why: Existing client, but 'sometime in the next few weeks' is not a deadline. This is the case that disproves 'existing clients are automatically high'.

inb-013.why: Referred by an existing client, so high value and not unsolicited — but 'soon' is not a deadline. Structurally identical to inb-007.
